nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger.measurement: Per player: counting games = games with minutes >= 20, plus up to 2 games with 15-20 minutes (verified 2025-26 rule: 20+ minutes in at least 63 of the 65 games, 15+ in the other two); slack = games_remaining - (65 - counting); P(ledger) = P(missed or sub-threshold games among remaining <= slack) under a Poisson-binomial with per-game miss probability = player-season availability rate shrunk with k=20 games toward the position prior, updated nightly after the 6pm ET injury report; P(eligible) = P(ledger) + (1 - P(ledger)) x P(appeal granted) from nba.eligibility_appeal_grant_model. As-of: last completed game. Governed awards (verified): MVP, DPOY, Most Improved, All-NBA, All-Defensive; ROY, Sixth Man and All-Rookie exempt; not applied to monthly awards, Coach/Executive of the Year, All-Star or draft markets; Clutch POY coverage unconfirmed (flag).

nba.games_played_eligibility.measurement: Per award, encode the season's governing rule from the league criteria: 65-game minimum (20+ minutes in 63, 15-20 minutes allowed in two) for MVP, DPOY, Most Improved, All-NBA and All-Defensive (verified 2025-26, no change reported for 2026-27); none for ROY, Sixth Man, All-Rookie; flag Clutch as unconfirmed. Track counting games and games remaining vs the threshold via nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger, add the Extraordinary Circumstances challenge branch from nba.eligibility_appeal_grant_model, and flag candidates within 5 games of the line.

nba.allstar_fan_vote_composite.label: All-Star starter composite (fan 50% / player 25% / media 25%), positionless top five per conference
nba.allstar_fan_vote_composite.mechanism: Starters are the five best weighted-average ranks per conference without regard to position (2026 rules): each candidate's rank in the fan, current-player and media votes is combined 50/25/25 and the fan vote breaks composite ties.
nba.allstar_fan_vote_composite.measurement: For each candidate and conference compute composite = 0.50 x fan_rank + 0.25 x player_rank + 0.25 x media_rank over all positions (verified for 2026: positionless, fan vote breaks ties, as with Wembanyama over Edwards in the West); fan_rank at close = last published early-return rank plus a random-walk adjustment scaled by the share of voting window remaining (step variance from past return snapshots), prior from last year's final fan rank, market size and social following; player and media ranks from the production rank in nba.award_stats with beta noise from past ballot-vs-stat rank gaps; starters = five lowest composites per conference; 10,000 draws, P(starter) per candidate. Use the 2027 rules when announced; until then the 2026 rules apply.
nba.allstar_fan_vote_composite.rationale: KXNBAASSTARTERS, KXNBAALLSTARS and KXNBAALLSTAR are not decided by the ballot of about 100 media voters in stage s4: the fan vote carries half the weight, is public in early-return snapshots during the voting window, and depends on market size and social following, while the player and media votes follow production. Since 2026 the five starters per conference are chosen without regard to position, so displacement is conference-wide and then by the 16 US / 8 international minimum, not between guard and frontcourt slots.

nba.allstar_reserve_coach_vote.label: All-Star reserve selection by coaches (7 per conference, positionless) and Commissioner replacements
nba.allstar_reserve_coach_vote.mechanism: After starters are fixed, each conference's head coaches vote seven reserves without regard to position (not their own players), the Commissioner names injury replacements and, under the USA-vs-World format, adds players to meet the 16 US / 8 international minimum.
nba.allstar_reserve_coach_vote.measurement: For each non-starter candidate: coach-vote score = z-score of production rank (nba.award_stats) plus team win% rank, calibrated by logistic regression on 10 seasons of reserve selections with conference strata only (positionless since 2026; earlier seasons had position slots, so fit with a pre/post-2026 indicator); P(reserve) = P(rank among the 7 conference reserve slots after starters are removed) via 10,000 draws conditional on the starter simulation; then apply the nationality minimum from nba.allstar_nationality_quota; injury replacement = P(a selectee is injured) x P(Commissioner picks the next-ranked player of the same conference).

nba.cross_league_title_combo.measurement: P_NBA from nba.title_path (at least 10,000 bracket draws, as-of the quote timestamp); P_NHL from the NHL catalog at the same timestamp: seeds from nhl.season_sim_distribution, bracket from nhl.bracket_path_difficulty, each series from nhl.series_context, giving P(named NHL team wins the Stanley Cup); both legs must use snapshots taken within the same nightly run (as-of = min of the two model timestamps). Joint = P_NBA x P_NHL, independence checked on historical seasons (correlation of title indicators for same-metro NBA/NHL pairs, expected near zero). Also output P(both alive after each round) from the two round-survival curves and set the value to zero at either elimination.

nba.tiebreak_ledger.measurement: For each team pair keep season-to-date head-to-head, division and conference records, record vs playoff-eligible teams in each conference, and net points, updated nightly. In the simulation apply the league order (NBA.com standings page): two-team ties - head-to-head, division leader over non-leader, division record (same division only), conference record, record vs playoff-eligible own-conference teams, record vs playoff-eligible other-conference teams, net points; three or more teams - division leader, head-to-head winning percentage among all tied teams, division record (all same division), conference record, record vs playoff-eligible own-conference teams, net points (no other-conference step). Whether a reduced multi-team tie re-enters the two-team procedure is not confirmed: compute both variants and report the difference, and re-read the 2026-27 standings page text. Output P(win tie) per pair and seed. As-of: nightly after final scores.

nba.division_race_tiebreak_state.label: Division-race state (view of nba.tiebreak_ledger inside nba.standings_sim)
nba.division_race_tiebreak_state.mechanism: Duplicate of nba.tiebreak_ledger: division winner contracts are read off the same simulated standings and the same official tiebreak order; this id is kept only as the division-level view of that ledger and must not be built separately.
nba.division_race_tiebreak_state.measurement: No separate computation: P(division winner) = share of nba.standings_sim season paths in which the team finishes first in its division after ties are resolved by nba.tiebreak_ledger; report the tie contribution separately. As-of: after each game.

nba.standings_sim.measurement: Single shared regular-season path simulation for every season-level archetype: 20,000 seasons of the remaining schedule, game by game in date order, from team ratings with posterior uncertainty (common within a season draw), home advantage, rest and injury scenarios; store each path's game-level results so season_futures_team (win totals, records, seeds, divisions via nba.tiebreak_ledger, play-in) and season_stat_markets (streaks via nba.team_win_streak_hazard and nba.longest_streak_max_and_tie_model, last unbeaten) read the same draws; output seed pmf and series inputs to nba.title_path. As-of: nightly after final scores.

nba.team_win_streak_hazard.measurement: View of the shared season paths: for each team, P(run of >= 20 consecutive wins at some point) = share of nba.standings_sim paths whose game sequence (current run carried in, Cup group and knockout games before the final counted, play-in and playoffs excluded) contains such a run; an exact dynamic-programming recursion on the same per-game probabilities (state = run length 0..19, absorbing 20) is the check for each team, and head-to-head games are consistent across teams because they come from the same path. As-of: nightly.

nba.title_path.measurement: Shared playoff bracket simulation for the bracket-level consumers attached to it (season_futures_team, series_and_cup, player_milestones for KXNBAPLAYOFF3D, the playoff single-game points archetype, awards_draft and parlay_combo): 50,000 draws; seeds from nba.standings_sim paths, play-in from nba.play_in_path_model, each series simulated game by game with the per-series kernel of nba.series_length_distribution (p_g from playoff ratings, 2-2-1-1-1 home court, injury state, series dependence); store per-path series lengths, venues and advancement so these consumers read the same draws. Single-series contracts whose matchup is already set (series cumulative points, per-series length markets) use the kernel directly; it equals title_path's conditional for that series. Output P(reach round r), P(title), opponents and games played per team. As-of: nightly.

nba.cup_format.measurement: 2026-27 format (verified NBA.com/ESPN): six groups of five, group winners plus one wild card per conference (best non-winner, wild-card ties start at point differential) seeded 1-4 per conference; quarterfinals 1v4 and 2v3 hosted by the higher seed; semifinals at the higher seed's arena (Dec 8-9); final neutral at Hinkle Fieldhouse, Indianapolis (Dec 11). Enumerate remaining group games with margin simulation and the group tiebreak order (nba.cup_group_tiebreak_state), then knockout games with home court for the higher seed through the semifinal and none in the final; Cup final excluded from regular-season stats.
nba.cup_format.mechanism: Cup outcomes depend on group-stage point-differential tiebreakers, wildcard rules and single-elimination knockout games hosted by the higher seed through the semifinal, with a neutral-site final (2026-27: Hinkle Fieldhouse).
nba.cup_format.rationale: Group-stage point differential makes blowout margins matter in Cup games, and group games count in the regular-season standings while the final does not; rest decisions and star availability vary relative to regular-season games. In 2026-27 the quarterfinals and semifinals are home games for the higher seed and only the final is neutral, so seeding carries home court. Rules change by season and must be re-read from official documentation.

nba.cup_finals_pair_probability.measurement: P(team reaches final) = P(qualifies as group winner or wild card) x P(wins quarterfinal) x P(wins semifinal), from team ratings with home-court advantage for the higher seed in both the quarterfinal and the semifinal (2026-27: semifinals at the higher seed's arena, verified), with rest-days adjustment; East and West brackets are disjoint until the final, so P(pair) = P(A reaches final) x P(B reaches final) with no shared-venue correlation; the final itself is at neutral Hinkle Fieldhouse. Re-read the season's Cup rules each year; as-of nightly during the Cup.
nba.cup_finals_pair_probability.mechanism: The Cup Finals pair is formed by the two semifinal winners, one from each conference bracket (the knockout bracket is split by conference), so the pair probability is a product of two independent single-elimination outcomes.
nba.cup_finals_pair_probability.rationale: The matchup contract resolves immediately upon qualification, not when the game is played; its probability depends on group results and quarterfinal and semifinal games hosted by the higher seed (2026-27), so seeding matters through home court; East and West halves share no games before the final.

nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.measurement: 2026 format (official NBA rules PDF, ak-static.cms.nba.com 2026-Kia-Shooting-Stars-Rules.pdf, sha256 ed035e65...b921): four teams of three, two current players plus one legend; seven locations shot in order 1 to 7 (right-lane layup/dunk 2, 18-ft right baseline 2, right elbow 2, right-wing three 3, top of the key 2, left-corner three 3, long-range three 4); each player takes one shot at each of locations 1-6 in the team's declared order, then at location 7 players shoot in that order as many times as the clock allows; a passer feeds each shot; the team advances as a unit; 1:10 clock; round 1 all four teams, top two to the final; the lower round-1 team shoots first in the final and round-1 scores do not carry. Current players: P(make) by spot from nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile. Legend component: last five career seasons' 3P% and FT% with an age discount of 1.5 points of 3P% per year since retirement, shrunk to the past legends' contest make rate with k = 50 shots; a shot-tempo term for the legend's attempts within the clock. Score = 2*(makes at locations 1, 2, 3, 5) + 3*(makes at locations 4, 6) + 4*(makes at location 7); a shot out of declared order scores zero and (locations 1-6) its shooter does not shoot again, and a team that does not have all three players make valid attempts at a location, or that shoots from locations out of order, is disqualified. Round-1 ties that decide advancement go to a 30-second rerun among only the tied teams (round-1 scores ignored); a tied final is rerun for the full 1:10. Simulate 20,000 contests under this rule set and report P(win) with a disqualification and out-of-order branch; the number of location-7 attempts per player inside 70 seconds and the legend's rate remain estimates (EMPIRICAL_QUESTION), and the Kalshi-specific treatment of disqualification, replay and cancellation stays unknown.
nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.rationale: Kalshi's rules give only team and date; the league's official 2026 Shooting Stars rules PDF (read and hashed 2026-11-09) gives the full format: four teams of three (two current players plus one legend), seven locations in fixed order worth 2/2/2/3/2/3/4 points, 1:10 clock, top two of four advance, 30-second first-round tiebreaker, full 1:10 final tiebreaker, disqualification and out-of-order rules. What stays unknown is only how Kalshi applies those rules to settlement. Legends have no current shooting data, so team skill mixes current catch-and-shoot rates with old evidence; tempo matters as in the 3PT contest.

nba.asg_mvp_vote_model.measurement: 2026 rule: media panel vote right after the championship game combined with a 25% in-game fan vote; scope = the whole tournament (Edwards 2026, totals across three games, 10 of 14 panel votes). Panel part: P(panel pick) = sum over teams P(team wins the tournament) from nba.asg_tournament_path_sim x conditional logit over that team's players on tournament points share, made threes, minutes, home-market flag and prior All-Star MVP (fit on 20+ events), plus a residual for a non-champion MVP from the historical share; final score = 0.75 x panel share + 0.25 x nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share; multiply by P(participates). As-of: final rosters.

nba.series_length_distribution.mechanism: The number of games in a best-of-seven series is a function of per-game win probability, home pattern and dependence between games; this is the per-series kernel that nba.title_path calls inside each bracket draw.
nba.series_length_distribution.measurement: Per-series kernel: P(series ends in k games) by dynamic programming over home pattern 2-2-1-1-1 with per-game win probabilities from own-model playoff ratings and a series dependence parameter (game-to-game correlation about +0.05 on margin, estimated from 2000-2025 playoff series), injuries as of the as-of date; output P(4..7) and P(win). For a set matchup this is used directly; for bracket-level contracts the same kernel is evaluated inside nba.title_path draws, so lengths and advancement are consistent across archetypes.

nba.governance_approval_pipeline.measurement: For each live deal record stage, date entered, and the historical distribution of days to the next stage from past NBA and other major-league sales (log-normal fit per stage, shrunk to cross-league pooled values with k=3 deals); compute P(reach required stage by T) = product of P(transition) x P(duration sum <= T-t); update when a stage is entered; apply the league approval threshold as a feasibility gate: three-quarters of governors (23 of 30), verified for the 25 Mar 2026 expansion-exploration vote.

nba.award_role_filters.measurement: Per award and as-of date compute boolean eligibility from the league definition stored per season: Sixth Man = games_off_bench > games_started (Sixth Man is exempt from the 65-game rule, verified 2025-26); ROY = first-year player on the league rookie list (exempt); Clutch POY = clutch minutes (last 5 minutes, margin within 5) >= the published minimum for that season (read from rules text, else 25th percentile of the prior season). Candidates then ranked by the stat the award names: clutch net points per 100 clutch possessions, BPM delta vs prior season (MIP, min 500 minutes both seasons), DWS per 36 (DPOY), each shrunk to season value with prior weight 10 games. Output candidate list and gap to the leader.
